problems.issue: The Pumpkin Prince is filed as a standalone event (kind 'other') with its own occurrences. The wiki calls him the main antagonist and boss of Super Spooktacular, and the wiki's Super Spooktacular page lists 'stopping the Pumpkin Prince' as one of the parent's objectives. The Prince's dates are just the parent's October runs, so the record duplicates or mis-scopes the parent event rather than being a sub-event of it.
problems.fix: Merge the Prince into the Super Spooktacular record as a world-event sub-activity (wiki: Pumpkin Prince; Super Spooktacular; Events). Keep the parent's dated runs (the answer's own open list gives 2009, 2010, 2011, 2013). Do not schedule the Prince as its own event.

problems.issue: The claim that the Prince world event ran inside the 2011 run (Oct 13 - Nov 23) is attributed to article 2304. The pack gives that article only for the parent run dates, and no Prince content is shown from it, so the Prince-specific link is unverified.
problems.fix: Cite the 2011 dates to the parent Super Spooktacular only, and state that the Prince's 2011 presence is unconfirmed.

problems.issue: The 2010 occurrence is month-level, and articles 1857, 1860 and 1861 repeat 1854 and are not independent. The 'recurring: null' field is defensible, but the 'Prince' occurrence is built only on undated Prince posts, so it cannot stand as a Prince occurrence.
problems.fix: Keep 2010 as a parent-event month only (article 1845), with the Prince presence marked unverified; no Prince occurrence list until a dated source exists.

problems.issue: The zone list omits the quest-line locations the client itself names. Locale 415330 places the Prince's tomb in Blackspore, and locale 416780 places the Ghost Hunter appearances in Sacred Grove. The list also includes Bone Bog Cemetery as a zone even though the answer says it is a members instance, not a world-event zone.
problems.fix: Zones: Snowhill, Stillwater Crossing and Bristlewood (locales 416782, 416783, 416809-416811) for world spawns; Sacred Grove (locale 415330, 416779-416780) and Blackspore (locale 415330, wiki Blackspore Swamp) for the quest and Dance-off; Bone Bog Cemetery (wiki) for the instance.

problems.issue: The Vampire vs. Werewolf Dance-off is listed as a Prince activity with items, but the items are wiki-only and undated. The wiki also says the Dance-off is hosted by the Prince in Blackspore during the parent event. This is a parent-event activity, not a separately dated Prince activity.
problems.fix: Attach the Dance-off to the Super Spooktacular parent with the note 'wiki-only, undated'. Drop the item list from the Prince record.

problems.issue: live 'unsure' and confidence 0.4 are honest. The answer still says the Prince is 'a boss and world-event sub-event' in its open list while the top-level record says kind 'other', so the record contradicts itself.
problems.fix: Set kind to the parent's holiday type and mark the Prince as a sub-activity of Super Spooktacular, with live unknown and no standalone schedule.

problems.issue: The exact 2011 run dates are cited to articleId=2304, but no index text I could search (articles, wiki) shows those dates. The only 2304 text I could see is the Prince event description (ghosts, Ghost Hunters in Snowhill, Stillwater Crossing, Bristlewood), with no dates. The dates are unsupported by any source I could check.
problems.fix: Keep 2011 as a year-level occurrence unless article 2304's date text is quoted. Cite the exact run dates only from a quote that shows them. The 2009 parent dates (articleId=476) are a separate parent-event claim and do not belong to the Prince record.

problems.issue: The October 2010 month is cited to articleId=1845, which is not among the pack's article summaries and was not confirmed by my lookups. The 1854 post itself is undated, so the month rests on an unseen source.
problems.fix: Mark the 2010 occurrence as unverified until article 1845 is quoted with its date, or drop the month and say 'undated, 2nd annual per article 1854'.

problems.issue: The answer says Lucinda helps defeat the Prince in Bone Bog Cemetery, citing locale 415338. The text I retrieved (415338) says 'Meet me in Bone Bog Cemetery, and I'll help you send that pumpkin-faced prince back', with no speaker name shown. The Lucinda attribution is not confirmed by that line.
problems.fix: Confirm the speaker of locale 415338 from the NPC/dialog record before naming Lucinda. Otherwise write 'an NPC (speaker unnamed in the text)'.

problems.issue: Verified: locale 415330 places the tomb in Blackspore, sealed by spectral guardians near the warpstones across Sacred Grove. The title (415331) is confirmed. This claim is correct.

problems.issue: The answer says no 2009 Prince occurrence is recorded and that the Prince's 2009 presence is not verified. But article 476 (the 2009 Super Spooktacular post the answer already cites for parent dates) is indexed as a Prince world event: 'Ghost Hunters in Snowhill, Stillwater Crossing and Bristlewood are world events for scaring off the Pumpkin Prince's ghosts' (articles fact:event, articleId=476). So a 2009 occurrence is supported and was missed.
problems.fix: Add a 2009 occurrence (Oct 14 - Nov 11, 2009, inside the Super Spooktacular run) sourced to http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=476, and drop the 'no 2009 Prince occurrence' open note.

problems.issue: Article 2304 is a real source (indexed as a Prince world event with Ghost Hunters in Snowhill, Stillwater Crossing, Bristlewood), but the evidence pack does not include it and the 'Oct 13 - Nov 23, 2011' dates are not visible in any source I could check. problems.fix: Confirm the Oct 13 - Nov 23, 2011 dates by reading articleId=2304 directly before keeping them; otherwise mark the 2011 occurrence as year-level only, like 2010.

problems.issue: The record is kept as a standalone 'other' event while its own open notes say it is a sub-event of Super Spooktacular and that the parent should be a separate record. Its occurrences are the parent's runs, so the calendar would show a Prince event with no dated parent to hang on. The Prince's recurrence is also unverified, yet recurring is null with no note that the parent's yearly pattern is the only candidate.
problems.fix: Attach the Prince as a child of the Super Spooktacular parent (dated runs 2009, 2010, 2011, 2013 from articles 476, 1845, 2304, 2949) and mark the Prince's per-year presence as per-occurrence, not inferred recurrence.

open: Recurrence: only 2012 is dated by a source in the pack. The wiki 'Birthday Bash' page calls it annual, but no second dated article is in the pack, and the wiki 'Cakenstein' page says he appears in 'the only Birthday Bash'. Recurrence is unconfirmed, so recurring is null.
Launch-day conflict: article 2107 gives April 28 as the anniversary; article 2580 and the wiki give April 29. Not resolved.
Cakeling helpers: named in article 2107 (Portuguese, 2011-era party post) and the wiki. Not attached to the 2012 Bash because no 2012 source in the pack names them.

Mystery Meat storyline (article 1284, undated, 'relative to capture' date): seven cakes baked with Mystery Meat by Glerga, Cakenstein fought with cakelings, fireworks mechanic. Treated as a SEPARATE, unscheduled Cakenstein storyline, not the Bash. Its quests (Cakenstein's Last Stand, Cakey Clue, Downing Cakenstein, Mysteriously Cakey Remains, Undelivered Confections) are not attached to the Bash. Its live status and dates are unknown.

2011 second-anniversary party (article 2107, Portuguese): the pack gives no year, only a relative date ('1 month, 1 week ago'), and says the party runs until May 18. It is NOT merged into the Bash and NOT scheduled here. Its Camellia party quests, eight zone birthday cakes and Boss Cake belong to that separate occurrence, pending a year check. The 'Anniversary Party' alias is dropped as unsourced.

Not listed, unsourced for 2012: 'Cakenstein Attacks!' encounter, Balloon Bow/Hammer/Axe/Sword/Saw/Wand prize-wheel weapons (wiki only, undated), Cupcake Hat (garbled, undated), locale titles 'Birthday Bash!' and 'Free Realms Turns Three!', birthday furniture bundle and decor (name ties only), and Queensfields / General Glowlight (locale-only lead). Pinata pet names, prices and currency are not in the pack.
Fireworks mechanic: sourced only to undated article 1284 and locale text. Not a dated Bash activity.
2013 occurrence (article 2924) was not in the evidence pack and is dropped.
Localized boss names (Kuchenstein / Gâtostein) are unverified and not listed.
Only the 2012 occurrence is scheduled. The other Cakenstein items above need year checks before they are added to the calendar.

problems.issue: locale:707 is quest description text, not a quest title. The answer labels it as the quest 'Stop Cakenstein and the cakelings disrupting the celebration'. The locale only shows that as the body of the description, so the title is not confirmed.
problems.fix: Cite locale:707 as the description of the Sacred Grove bake-off quest (Camellia near the great tree in Sanctuary starts it). Give the quest title only if a title id is found.

problems.issue: locale:706 'Free Realms Turns Three!' is a 2012 name tie, not a Bash quest title confirmed by a source. The answer does flag it as a name tie, which is fair, but it still sits in the quest list.
problems.fix: Keep it under open/name-tie only, or confirm it against the quest table. Locale 695 ('Birthday Bash 2012 marks the 3rd Anniversary of Free Realms') is the stronger 2012 tie and should be cited for the year.

problems.issue: The answer cites only article 2107 for 2011, but the pack's lookup also has article 2099 (German, freerealms.com, 'second birthday party', running from the post date until May 18, anniversary April 28, boss 'Kuchenstein' with cakelings). That is a second 2011 source the answer omits, and it also corroborates the May 18 end date independently of the relative-dated post.
problems.fix: Add http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=2099 as a 2011 source (second-anniversary party, ends May 18; Kuchenstein with cakelings).

problems.issue: Merging the 2011 'Anniversary Party' into the same yearly series as the 2012 Birthday Bash rests on the answer's inference. The 2011 posts name a 'Kuchenstein' boss and use 'birthday party' wording, while 2012 is 'Birthday Bash'. This is reasonable but not explicitly sourced as one series.
problems.fix: Keep the alias but state it as an inference: the 2011 and 2012 posts both mark the launch anniversary (April 28/29) with a party, a cake boss and Camellia's party quests. Locale 695 is the only text tying the 'Birthday Bash' name to a specific year (2012).

problems.issue: The wiki prize-wheel pages and locale 4917 tie 'Cakenstein Attacks!' to the annual Bash. Locale 4917 is the title, so this is supported. But the claim 'the prize-wheel encounter during the annual Birthday Bash' rests only on wiki text, which the answer lists correctly.
problems.fix: No change needed; the wiki pages are cited correctly. Note the source is wiki-only.

problems.issue: The Birthday Bash Furniture Bundle (locale:691/692, 1350 station_cash) and the decor items (locale:666, 436980-436983) are listed as event items on name tie alone. The answer itself says they are undated and name-tie only, and no source ties them to a Bash occurrence. They should not sit in the event's item list.
problems.fix: Remove them from the event's items, or move them to an 'unassigned name-tie' note. Only items with a source tying them to a dated occurrence belong here: the Birthday Cake hat (article 2580, 2012), the four pinata pets (article 2580, 2012), the eight zone cakes and Boss Cake (article 2107, 2011), the Balloon prize-wheel weapons (wiki Balloon pages, 'annual Birthday Bash', undated), and the Cupcake Hat (wiki, 'available during the Birthday Bash event', undated).

problems.issue: 'Birthday Bash! (locale:29341)' is listed as a quest of the event on name tie only. 'Free Realms Turns Three! (locale:706)' is also a name tie to the 2012 3rd birthday, with no source in the pack saying the quest belongs to the Bash. 'Stop Cakenstein and the cakelings disrupting the celebration (locale:707)' has no source in the pack at all.
problems.fix: Keep only quests with a source tying them to the Bash: 'Cakenstein Attacks!' (wiki Balloon pages say the prize wheel sits on this encounter 'during the annual Birthday Bash'). Mark the other three as unverified name ties, or drop them. Their locale ids should be checked against the locale table before they are cited.

problems.issue: The Mystery Meat / Cakenstein storyline (article 1284) is excluded from the Bash, and the pack's quest answers (Cakey Clue, Downing Cakenstein, Mysteriously Cakey Remains, Undelivered Confections, Cakenstein's Last Stand) are marked live yes. The answer leaves them unassigned. The 1284 relative date ('3 years, 10 months ago' before capture) does not match the stated 2011-06-04 capture date, so the answer's dating of that article cannot be relied on. The answer also gives no assignment for these quests, though the cross notes are empty.
problems.fix: Keep the honest 'unassigned' status, but state that the 1284 date cannot be fixed from its relative wording, and that the Mystery Meat storyline may be an earlier, separate Cakenstein event (its date is unknown). Do not attach its quests to the Bash without a source.

problems.issue: The 'yearly in April' pattern rests on three dated instances (2011, 2012, 2013) plus wiki text. The 2011 instance has only a relative posting date and a capture date. The wiki Cakenstein page says he appears 'during the only Birthday Bash', which contradicts the annual pattern, and the answer flags this but still reports 'yearly' as settled.
problems.fix: Describe the recurrence as 'annual in April, confirmed for 2012 and 2013 by dated articles; 2011 inferred from the second-anniversary wording'. Keep the wiki 'only Birthday Bash' conflict in open.

problems.issue: The year 2011 is not in the evidence pack. Article 2107 has date null and only a relative posting date ('1 month, 1 week ago'). The pack gives no year. The answer assigns 2011 and a 'May 18, 2011' end date on that basis, which is an inference. The 'Anniversary Party' alias is also inferred and not sourced.
problems.fix: Record the 2107 party as a Portuguese second-anniversary post with an undated, relative capture and an end date of May 18, with no year assigned. Keep 2011 only as an open item until the year is verified from the article itself.

problems.issue: The 2013 April 29 occurrence cites article 2924, which is not in the evidence pack and is marked 'not re-read in this pass'. Nothing in the pack supports it, so it is unsupported here.
problems.fix: Drop the 2013 occurrence from this evidence set or cite the article text directly. Do not rely on the prior pass.

problems.issue: 'Annual in April' is a pattern drawn from two dated posts (2012, and the 2013 unverified one) plus an undated 2011 post. The wiki 'annual event' wording is secondary. The pack's Cakenstein wiki text also says he appears in 'the only Birthday Bash', which contradicts the annual pattern.
problems.fix: State the recurrence as unconfirmed beyond 2012 until a second dated source is in the pack. Report the wiki contradiction as an open item, not as support.

problems.issue: The 2011 second-anniversary party (article 2107) is listed as an alias of the Birthday Bash. It is a separate occurrence: article 2107 says the anniversary is April 28 and the party ends May 18, and the second anniversary is 2011. Folding it into the Bash name merges two occurrences under one event. The answer's own open note admits no source ties the two by name.
problems.fix: Remove the 'Second-anniversary party' alias. Record the 2011 party (article 2107, Portuguese, year inferred from 'second anniversary', end May 18) as its own occurrence, or leave it unscheduled. Do not attach Camellia's quests, the eight zone cakes or the Boss Cake to the 2012 Bash without a 2012 source.

problems.issue: 'Cakenstein event' and 'Cakenstein Attacks!' are aliases of the Bash, but article 1284 describes a separate Cakenstein event (Mystery Meat cakes, fireworks, undated, relative date '3 years, 10 months ago'). The answer's own open list says it may be a separate storyline. The event name 'Birthday Bash (... Cakenstein world event)' therefore merges the Mystery Meat storyline with the Bash.
problems.fix: Split the Cakenstein Mystery Meat storyline (article 1284, undated; quests Cakenstein's Last Stand, Cakey Clue, Downing Cakenstein, Mysteriously Cakey Remains, Undelivered Confections) into its own unscheduled event. Keep the Bash as the 2012 world event (article 2580, 2012-04-26; TenTonHammer 2012-04-30) only.

problems.issue: Recurrence is not justified. Only 2012 is dated by a source. The 'annual' claim rests on one wiki sentence, and the wiki 'Cakenstein' page says he appears 'during the only Birthday Bash', which contradicts it. The answer still sets live: 'yes' and a pattern-based name.
problems.fix: Schedule only the dated 2012 occurrence: Apr 26 to May 24, 2012 (article 2580; TenTonHammer 2012-04-30 confirms the May 24 end). Mark recurrence as unconfirmed. Do not extend to other years until a second dated source is found.

problems.issue: 'Cakenstein Attacks!' and the Balloon prize-wheel weapons are attached to the Bash from undated wiki pages. The Balloon pages say 'during the annual Birthday Bash' with no year, so the link to 2012 is not sourced. Cupcake Hat is also undated and garbled.

problems.issue: The eight zone birthday cakes and Boss Cake are attached to the Bash, but the source is article 2107 (2011 party). They belong to the 2011 occurrence.

50% off Station Cash purchases of 2000 Station Cash or more during Super Fan Days.

open: Critique fix applied: the alias 'Super Fan Discount! (locale:432670, ...)' is removed. Aliases now hold only 'Super Fan Days'. Locale 432670 ('Super Fan Discount!') is an unconfirmed candidate: no article links it to this event yet. Confirm before adding it as an alias.
Only one occurrence (Nov 3-9, 2010) is sourced. No article says it recurs, so recurring is null. Other years were searched in articles and none came up.

Name collision: the lookup also returns other '[Super Fan]' events that are separate promotions and must not merge into this one: 'Super Fan Summer Sizzle' (article 2218, last day Aug 18, 2011) and 'Super Fan Holidays' (article 1939, a member triple discount). The pack may have merged these under the name 'Super Fan', so treat them as different events.
Items: no daily item is named in any source. The one-day sale items and their prices are unknown, and the in-game discount percentage is not stated. Items is empty.
Zones, NPCs, quests and rewards: none sourced.
Article 1883 is cited in evidence from the earlier answer. It did not come up in this lookup, so re-check its quote before relying on it. The same date is independently in 1880, 1884 and 1885.
Pack articles 1896 and 1897 date the event only by relative 'posted 7 months ago' stamps. The year is taken from 1880 and 1884, not from those stamps.
Live status is yes from past-tense articles ('ran', 1880 and 1884). 1885 and 1895 are announcement wording. The run dates are stated in articles, so this is treated as live.

problems.issue: The second alias is a guess. Locale 432670 resolves via ids to 'Super Fan Discount!' (kind other), and no article ties that string to this event, as the answer's own open[2] admits. The parenthetical note is also packed into the alias string, so a calendar would read it as a literal alias name.
problems.fix: Remove 'Super Fan Discount! (locale:432670...)' from aliases. Keep only 'Super Fan Days'. Record locale 432670 as an unconfirmed candidate in open, with no source tying it to the event, until an article links the two.

problems.issue: The answer says the in-game discount percentage is not stated. The pack's own summaries for articles 1895 and 1896 say the daily one-day item sale was 50% off (1896: 'a daily 50%-off in-game item from November 3 to November 9'). The quoted lines in the pack do not contain 50%, so this is a summary-only claim, but the answer's 'not stated' is too strong. Nothing is wrong with the dates or the item-less state.
problems.fix: Record the daily item sale as 'one specially selected item per day, Nov 3-9 2010, reported as 50% off in the pack summaries of articles 1895 and 1896 (quote not verified, so not confirmed)'. Keep Items empty until an article names an item. Source: lookup of articles 1884 (economy fact), 1895 and 1896 summaries in n026.json.

problems.issue: The open note says article 1883 is cited in the earlier answer's evidence and needs a re-check, but 1883 is not in this answer's evidence list. Its text does support the daily one-day sale claim (lookup: 'Each participating game, including Free Realms, had a one-day special sale on a single item each day').
problems.fix: Either add 1883 to evidence with that quote, or drop the stale note. The daily-sale claim is already supported by articleId=1884 ('daily one-day sale on one specially selected item... starting Wednesday') and by 1880 and 1885, so the claim itself stands.

problems.issue: Timing is known (Wed 3 Nov to Tue 9 Nov 2010, one occurrence, sourced by 1880, 1884, 1885, 1895). What it adds is not known: no daily item is named and the discount percentage on items is not stated, so 'what it adds' is incomplete.
problems.fix: Keep wireable false until the daily items or the in-game discount are sourced, or mark the event as timing-only and wireable for the Station Cash 50% offer (articleId=1880) alone.

open: Stone Heart is the villain of this event, not a separate event. The pack's title and names_seen are 'Stone Heart', but the sources tie it to the Festival of Hearts. Stone Heart is an NPC in this record.

Zone conflict: article 2026 (French) places the festival in Joyful Valley, and articles 2018/2019 (Spanish) place it in Vegalegre with pixies named differently. Merry Vale is supported by 967, 969, 2016, 2500, 2501. These may be translation or regional variants, or separate runs. Unresolved.
No run end date for any year. TCG bundle year is undated (article 1009).
2011 run: only the wiki Cupid page names it; no article confirms the 2011 run or its month.
2012 occurrence rests on a wiki news archive entry for the update date; the festival's own 2012 start and end are not confirmed.
Articles 2498 and 2499 say the festival launched on PS3 on the post day; platform scope for the 2012 run is unverified.

Quests: only Softening the Stone and Stone Heart's Hideaway are tied to the festival by quest answers (Stone Heart's Hideaway is live 'unsure'). Sabotage For Safety, Under Pressure and It's Too Quiet... appear in quest answers that mention Stone Heart, but I have not verified a Festival of Hearts tie for them, so they are left out. Potent Love Potion, Sleeping Pixie, Dubawug's Sweetheart, Where is the Love?, Ooey, Gooey Love, A Tale of Two Hearts, A Bundle of Love, Petal Picker and Potion Testing were not re-verified and are left out. The Dove pet pal reward was tied to Sleeping Pixie, so it is dropped until that quest is verified.
'Mending Hearts' (locale:427177) is a client string, not a confirmed quest; not listed.
Rylan and Arianna are legend pixies, not NPCs in this record.
Stone Heart's Pink Bear, Cupid, Heart Critter and Bowheart rest on wiki pages only; not checked against articles.
All prices are null: no source gives a price. Station Cash currency for the wiki item pages rests on their 'Station Cash Marketplace' text. Teddy Bear Costume was not checked and is omitted.

Client names not tied to an article or wiki page are omitted: Festival of Hearts Mystery Gift (locale:4418), Festival of Hearts Wheel (locale:400039), Stone Heart's Wing Pattern Card (locale:4781), Stone Hearted furniture (locales 3558-3570, 3575).
Festival de Corazones dance (articles 957/959/960, Friday 12 Feb 2010, Server 1) is a separate community event, not an occurrence of this festival. 'Corazon Petreo' is not an alias.
Heart Festival (article 976, Joyful Valley) is unverified as the same event and is not an alias.
Wireable: false. Start is sourced for 2010 (article 967, checked) and 2012 (wiki, update date only). No end date. No 2011 month. Zone conflict unresolved.

problems.issue: The 2011 and 2013 entries give the parent Super Spooktacular run dates (2011: Oct 13 - Nov 23, articleId=2304; 2013: Oct 1 - Nov 12, articleId=2949). evidence.claim: The 1st anniversary All Day Birthday Party ran as eight hourly parties, one per region, on Thursday April 29, 2010, 9am-5pm PDT, each doubling as an Ambassador Hide and Seek game.
The birthday party ran from the announcement until May 10, 2010, and the festivities were scheduled to end on 10 May 2010.
Parties were set up in eight zones named in English: Joyful Vale, Criqueville, Snow Hill, Misty Glade, Wugachug, Blackspore, Heather Moor and Sanctuary.
Camellia, near the great tree in Sanctuary, starts the birthday party quests, and other Sanctuary residents also give quests, including some members-only ones.
The party's cake boss Gatostein (English client name Cakenstein) must be defeated seven times during the birthday event; fireworks work against it.
Cakenstein is the result of a baking accident in Glerga's kitchen, a Robgoblin chef, when she added Mystery Meat to a bake-off recipe.
The official 1st anniversary guide lists daily activities: cake bake-off with Camellia, Flitter's invitation contest, Quills' balloon trade, Helga's feast ingredients and the Cakenstein boss fights.
Chef Jarvie in Happy Valley is part of the 1st anniversary celebration activities, per the guide.
Free Realms' 1st birthday celebration was set to begin April 29, 2010, with new in-game events and prizes to follow.
Birthday Party Crates were created for the first anniversary, contain party supplies, and were sold in the Marketplace.
Completing party quests yields birthday gifts; anniversary gifts include balloon weapons, t-shirts and illusions.

Eight party areas are named in German (Jubeltal, Sanddorf, Schneehugel, Schleierwiese, Wugachug, Pfifferdorf, Dornenwald, Freistatte) with players starting at Sanctuary (Freistatte). No source maps these German names to the English zone names.

open: Event identity: the 2010 1st-anniversary party (sourced by articles 1330 and 1267) and the Birthday Bash branding of 2012-2013 are linked only by theme and the anniversary. No source states they are one recurring event under one name. Treat as one anniversary series with a possible split; a reviewer should decide.
2010 start date unknown; only the 10 May 2010 end is stated (article 1330). Article 1267 is a summary, not re-read in full.
2011 year is inferred from 'second anniversary' wording; the end date 18 May comes from article 2099 (German). Article 2107 (Portuguese) not re-read.
2012 start date not stated; end 24 May 2012 (article 2580). 2013 end date not stated.
Start day unresolved: 28 April (articles 2107, 2098, 2580, tentonhammer) vs 29 April (article 2924, wiki). Human decision needed before scheduling.
Recurrence is an observed pattern across four years, not a stated rule. Do not schedule without the start day.

Zones: 2010 eight-zone set per article 1267 conflicts with client names (Misty Glade / Heather Moor vs Shrouded Glade / Seaside). Not reconciled. Sacred Grove, Happy Valley, Queensfields, Snowhill, etc. are not tied to one occurrence. Joyful Vale and Criqueville have no source.
Furniture bundle price 1350 Station Cash (locale:692) not re-verified in this pass; bundle membership of table, bed, chair, sofa not confirmed.
Cake item tie to the event rests on article 1267 summary and locale:14419. Per-cake descriptions not checked.
Quests not verified and omitted: A Piece of Cake, Undelivered Confections, Mysteriously Cakey Remains, Cakey Clue, To Bake a Pretty Cake. 'Birthday Cake Bake-off' is not a confirmed title.
Video refs (C3fysVLxrMg/00498, pJzcZTI1Pgk/00238, 0feIhpgdWOc/00126, a1p2wZhNao0/00014, mAyN-7xjr8s/00028) are carried from the pack and not re-checked.
Cakenstein is a monster, not an NPC; listed under npcs only because the pack did.

Excluded as unrelated: Waldo 25th Anniversary (locale 9144), guild anniversaries, Anniversary Ring (locale 66913), Birthday Invitation, Birthday Candle, Birthday Gift, Birthday Boomer (no tie to event).

Label 2010 ('1st anniversary birthday party', article 1267) and 2011 ('2nd anniversary birthday party', article 2099) as the same recurring anniversary series, not as the Birthday Bash by name, unless a source says otherwise.

problems.issue: Verified: article 1267 summary says the party ran from the posting day until May 10, 2010, with party areas in eight zones, Camellia quests in Sanctuary, and a cake-collecting reward from the boss. problems.issue: Verified: article 2099 (German) says the second anniversary (anniversary April 28) party runs from the post date until May 18. I did not re-check article 2107's Portuguese 'dia 18 de maio' wording. The year 2011 is derived from 'second anniversary' wording, as stated.

The answer's own note says article 1267 names Misty Glade and Heather Moor, which conflicts with Shrouded Glade and Seaside.
problems.fix: Split zones per occurrence: 2010 = the eight zones of article 1267 (names not reconciled with client names); 2013 = Sanctuary only (article 2924); 2012 = Sanctuary plus the cake-zone set as sourced. Do not present the 11-zone list as one event's zones.

evidence.claim: Summer Camp 2010 was a themed community event season. It ran 13 weeks from the announcement week, in summer 2010.

Each week of Summer Camp celebrated a different theme. Fashion Week was the theme of one of those weeks, with fashion shows held through the week and activities for showing off wardrobes with friends.
The Fashion Week post (undated in the pack) gives the same theme statement, with fashion shows during the week and friend activities.
Summer Camp is a community event season in which each week celebrates a different theme. Week themes named in articles include Arts and Crafts Week.
Sports Week (Semana Deportiva) and Crafting Week (Semana de Artesanias) are other theme weeks of the same Summer Camp season.
Crafting Week is another theme week of Summer Camp, with a new printable activity calendar each week.
Summer Camp was reached through a new Warpstone deep inside Greenwood Forest, placed for the summer season.
locale:442124 names the place Summer Camp.
A printable Summer Camp Activity Calendar was released with a new version each week.
The Summer Camp event added 14 new camp land quests, along with daily questlines and events.

Weekly community-event schedule: Tuesdays at 09:00 and 16:00, Thursdays at 15:00, and Friday mornings at 09:00, Pacific time. The article (dated 2010-07-01) states this schedule; it is the expected schedule, not a confirmed live time for each week.
The Summer Camp season ended with a Pet Parade called the last Summer Camp event.
Quest titles naming the Summer Camp season: Chatty's Summer Camp Party and Robbie's Summer Camp Party. The tie is by the title's name only; no article links them to a week.
Robbie's Summer Camp Party is a quest title with the Summer Camp name.
The NPC line 'Let's all go the fashion show!' names a fashion show. No article ties it to Fashion Week, so it is not counted as an item or quest here.

open: Split as the critique asks. This entry is the Summer Camp 2010 community season. Fashion Week is one theme week inside it, and the pack's combined name merged the two. Fashion Week needs its own calendar row only if the calendar tracks theme weeks; its exact week and dates are not stated in any source.

2012: exact dates unknown. The 2012 entry rests on a recap link and the Oct 11, 2012 update line only.
2009: the window is the pre-event schedule. Live run is supported only by the Oct 19, 2009 recap (node/75724), which I did not re-read.
Zone conflict for the dance-off: Blackspore Swamp (locale 5197, 436401) and Bone Bog Cemetery (articleId=1862) are consistent as zone and sub-location. articleId=1861 says Sporeshade; unresolved.
Halloween Harry: Sanctuary (about 30 client lines, article 1864) versus Pixiewood (locale 436401, 416800). Both appear in client text; not resolved.
Year-count conflict: articleId=2949 says 'Fourth Annual' for 2013, while 2009 'First Annual' and 2010 'second annual' imply 2013 is the fifth. Wording kept as quoted.

The dance-off storyline text (locale 432206, 432223, 432244, 432288, 432314, 432333) was cited by a critic and not re-read by me.

evidence.claim: Promotion: buying a Dog or Cat priced at 400 Station Cash gave a free matching doggy or kitty outfit.
Window stated in article 2521 as 12:01 AM Pacific Feb 10, 2012 to 11:59 PM Pacific Feb 14, 2012.

Independent corroboration of the window: article 2518 (German SOE promotion) runs 10 Feb 2012 09:01 to 15 Feb 2012 08:59 CET. CET is UTC+1 and PST is UTC-8, so this equals 10 Feb 00:01 to 14 Feb 23:59 Pacific. The year 2012 comes from these window texts, not a dated post.

Article 2521 names all 15 pets with their promo outfit: Dashes/Doggy Astro, Summer/Doggy Bridal, Peccadillo/Doggy Cardboard Bot, Diego/Doggy Dumptruck, Jinx/Doggy Fairy, Marlin/Doggy Panda, Allie/Doggy Sassy, Scooter/Doggy Tuxedo, Scout/Doggy Wizard, Hurricane/Doggy Wizard, Mr. Kitty/Kitty Astro, Pooky/Kitty Bridal, Kiri/Kitty Fairy, Gizmo/Kitty Panda, Luna/Kitty Sassy.

Article 2518 lists cat outfits with German pet names: Herr Kitty (astro), Prinzesschen (cheeky), Schneeflocke (wedding), Otis (fairy), Laeufer (panda). These match the Kitty Astro, Fairy and Panda pairings in article 2521.
Client strings name the event 'Valentine's Special' and the matching outfits for the same pets, with locale IDs 3673-3687.
Wiki Festival of Hearts is a separate Merry Vale February-March event (Stone Heart), not this promotion.
Ten Ton Hammer article on Valentine's in Runes of Magic is not Free Realms and is excluded.

open: Name and merge: the in-game 12 Days of Presents (2012, 2013) is Free Realms' component of SOE's 12 Days of Holidays. The wiki '12 Days of Presents' page says so directly, and locale:832 describes the umbrella promo, in which participating games feature a daily special. Merge as one event with a disambiguation note, or keep the umbrella promo as its own entry (its Free Realms-specific details are not in this pack). Article 2827 also uses the name '12 Days of Holidays', so that alias needs a note at merge time.
Articles 2440 and 2441 are not confirmed here (locale:2440 and locale:2441 are item strings, not articles), so no 2011 occurrence is claimed.
2012 year for the 12 Days Present and 12 Days Bow quest series rests on the articles and the wiki 2012 list, not on a client year string. The client titles have no year.

2013 exact dates are not in the pack. The Dec 13-24 window for 2013 rests on the wiki's annual wording and the undated client quest dialog locale:441963, not on a 2013 article. 2013 rewards are taken from the wiki 2013 list only.

Wiki Template:News 'Game Update 122.1' is dated 12/04/2013 in the lookup (the earlier critique said 12/03). The snippet that came back is truncated and does not show the claim that previous years' Snow Days content is active again, so that claim is not used here.

Snow Days Builders Pack appears in both the 2012 and 2013 wiki lists. Its year is left as 2012 with the ambiguity noted. Snow Days Gift Box - Cookies, Gift Box - Decorations and Unicorn Sweater are also in the wiki 2013 list, so their 2012 first appearance is kept and the 2013 re-listing is recorded in their source fields.
Snow Days is a seasonal name (wiki category), not a hard alias: the Winter Basin community party (articles 1953, 1958, 1962) is a different event that uses the same name.

The 2012 Day 1 to Day 12 present titles and the 2013 Day 1 to Day 12 titles are client strings. The pack summary title '12 Days Present - Day 1 through Day 12' is replaced by the exact client titles above.
Yearly recurrence rests on the wiki 'annual' wording plus two dated occurrences (2012 articles; 2013 client and wiki items). The 2013 window is unverified by a dated 2013 source.

Wiki 'Snow Days' also names NPCs Candi Ivy, Everett and Calvin Coldcastle and enemies (Abominable Snowman, Snowman, Crafty Robgoblins). None is tied to the 12 Days event in the checked evidence, so they are not listed in npcs.
Prices and currency are not in any source for these items; all set to null, and reward applies. 5,000 Coins is a reward amount, not a currency.
Live status: 2012 is live per articles 2813 and 2827. 2013 is live per client strings and wiki item pages, not an article, so yes is inferred for 2013.

Critique point on the articles index: the articles fact lookup does return 2813 and 2827 for the every-4 bonus and 15-present total, so the earlier claim that the lookup returned nothing does not hold. Both articles and the wiki are now cited for that rule.

Client NPC dialog ties the semi-formal dance to the Festival of Hearts: 'Wear your best outfit and join us for a Festival of Hearts semi-formal dance!'
Client string 'Scheduled: Community Event: Festival of Hearts Semi-formal' ties the semi-formal name to a scheduled community event.

Live status: confirmed as run. Article 960 reports the sessions as started, and article 959 reports it was held on 12 February 2010.

evidence.claim: Free Realms reached 1,000,000 registered players, and the team held a party to celebrate, on May 15th, 2009
The party was held at Snowhill, where players and team members gathered to hang out and dance
The wiki Bruce page dates the bash to Friday May 15, 2009 at 5pm Pacific, held by the Free Realms Ambassador team at Snowhill, and says it was reached within 17 days of launch
Crowds from the party gathered around the NPC Bruce at Snowhill
Client text search found no locale strings for this 1M Party; the only Snowhill party strings are other events (Snowhill Playground Party, Snow Day, Birthday Party, New Years Eve)
Article 1830 is a different community party on the Snowhill playground, so it is not this event

open: Kind is a judgement: this is a one-time milestone celebration hosted by the team, so 'other' is used rather than 'community'. Bryce should confirm the category.
Live is 'yes' because the article is a recap of a party already held on May 15th, 2009. No pre-launch preview was seen.
Recurring is null. Only one occurrence is sourced, and nothing says it recurs.
No items, rewards or quests are tied to this event by any source. The pack lists none, and client, wiki and article text show none.
Bruce is included as an NPC only from the wiki Bruce page, which places the crowd around him at the party. The article itself does not name him.
The pack's article date is null. The May 15th, 2009 date comes from the article summary and the article's own text, and the wiki page gives the same date.
The pack's wiki_category_members is empty, so no category page confirms the event. The 'Bruce' wiki page is the only wiki source.

evidence.claim: The client names the event 'Community Event: Memorial Caverns Pool Party' (locale 9108), which ties the name to the Memorial Caverns and to a community event category.

A community Memorial Caverns pool party was held in the pools below the Memorial Caverns, hosted by the Community Team, with high dives, dancing, silly string fights and swimming on Server 1. Its US/Latin America session was Thursday January 20th, 2011 at 3pm Pacific Time, and its UK/Europe session was Friday January 21st, 2011 at 9:00am Pacific Time, both on Server 1.

The French announcement gives the same sessions: Thursday 20 January 2011 at 3pm Pacific for US and Latin America, and Friday 21 January 2011 at 18:00 CET for UK and Europe, on Server 1. It adds duels to the activities. The article's own gloss reads 4:00 GMT for 18:00 CET, which conflicts with the Pacific time (see open).

The Spanish announcement gives the same dated sessions: Thursday 20 January 2011 at 15:00 Pacific Time (US and Latin America) and Friday 21 January 2011 at 09:00 Pacific Time (UK and Europe), on Server 1. It describes a pool party with dancing, confetti cannons and swimming in the pools beneath the Caverns of Memory. Its '16:00 European Time' gloss conflicts with 9am Pacific (see open).

Article 2003 places the Caverns of Memory in the depths of the Sanctuary caves, reached through the atlas and the Forgotten Caves battle. Its dates, server, community-team host and activities match the Memorial Caverns pool party, which supports treating Caverns of Memory as an alias. The article does not name Memorial Caverns, so the link rests on matching details rather than an explicit name.

The pack's 'Memorial Caverns collection updates' is an undated location note, not an event. Article 144 says only that collection updates are available inside Memorial Caverns. It is listed in open, not as this event's identity.
Memorial Caverns is a Sanctuary museum on Pixie and Sanctuary history, located north of the World Tree.

open: Time conflict in the sources. 9am Pacific in January (PST, UTC-8) is 17:00 GMT, which equals 18:00 CET. The recorded time for the UK/Europe session is 17:00 GMT = 18:00 CET = 9am Pacific. The sources' '4pm GMT' (articleId 2002) and '4:00 GMT' beside 18:00 CET (articleId 2007) conflict with their own Pacific and CET times, and articleId 2003's '16:00 European Time' also conflicts with 9am Pacific. The Jan 20 US/LatAm session (3pm Pacific = 23:00 GMT) is consistent.

The pack name 'Memorial Caverns collection updates' merges two things. The one-line collection-updates note (articleId 144, undated) is not an event. The event is the Memorial Caverns Pool Party (articleIds 2002, 2003, 2007), and the event name and aliases are the pool party.

The Caverns of Memory alias rests on matching details (same Jan 20/21 2011 sessions, Server 1, community team, dancing and swimming), not on an explicit name match, since articleId 2003 never names Memorial Caverns.

The pack's article dates are null. The dates above come from the article text. Article 2007 gives no publication date; the store's 'four and a half months before a June 2011 capture' remark is a capture-date note, not a publication date, so no publication date is stated.
Only one occurrence (January 2011, both sessions) is sourced. Nothing says it recurred, so recurring is null.

Live is 'yes' for the January 2011 sessions only, based on announcement text ('was held' in articles 2002 and 2007). The announcements do not confirm attendance, and a pre-launch preview would not count.

No item, price, currency, NPC, quest or reward is tied to the pool party by any source. The 'Memorial Caverns Explorer's ...' clothing and backpacks (locale 29150, 30259, 30996, 29388) and the Looking for Volunteers and tour quests are named after the place, not the event, and are excluded.

Time Left: 17 Hours'. A 'Party Pool' place also exists (locale 6633/6634). No source ties these to the January 2011 pool party. They may be a later or separate store or housing event, and this answer does not assert which.

problems.issue: The answer says article 2003 gives no date and is only a possible alias. The article text does give dates: US and Latin America on Thursday 20 January 2011 at 15:00 Pacific, and UK and Europe on Friday 21 January 2011 at 09:00 Pacific (16:00 CET), both on Server 1. It is the same pool party, and the answer omits it from the evidence list.

Remove the 'no date, unconfirmed alias' hedge. 'Caverns of Memory' is an alias of Memorial Caverns, since 2003 places the pool beneath the Caverns of Memory in the Sanctuary caves.

problems.issue: The answer infers that article 2007 was published around February 2011, before the event, from the store's note that it is about four and a half months before a June 2011 capture. That inference conflicts with the article itself, which announces a session on 20 January 2011, so publication must be before that date.
problems.fix: Do not state a publication date. The article is only known to announce the 20 and 21 January 2011 sessions (source: articleId 2007). The four-and-a-half-month note is a capture-date remark, not a publication date.

problems.issue: 'north of or behind the World Tree' adds 'behind', which the source does not say. Article 144 says only 'north of the World Tree'.

evidence.claim: Summer Camp was a community event season (2010) in which each week celebrated a different theme; Arts and Crafts Week was one.
Virtual Summer Camp was released June 7, 2010, shortly before the game passed 12 million registered users.
Free Realms ran the virtual Summer Camp themed events in summer 2010, for 13 weeks beginning the week of the announcement.
The season added 14 new camp land quests along with daily questlines and events.
Chatty created a camp deep inside Greenwood Forest, reached through a newly activated Warpstone.
A printable Summer Camp Activity Calendar was released with a new version each week.
Pet Parade was described as the last Summer Camp event.
Pirate's Plunder minigame in Seaside was the main focus of the Summer Camp Pirate Week.
Marshmallow pets were sold in the Summer Camp Marketplace and are only available during Summer Camp.

Marketplace items include marshmallow animals, Chatty and Robby inflatable decorations, a Spooky Campfire (grants a temporary ghost pet when clicked), and Talent Fragments with marshmallow campfire variants.
Quest titles Jojo's Mojo and Jojo's Dojo exist and their objectives name Summer Camp.
Glugmort is Jojo's father: the Jojo A-go-go objective says to deliver Glugmort's package to Jojo at the camp counselors.
Summer Camp is a client place name, and the Jojo quest text places Jojo at the camp near the Greenwood Forest warpstone.

A second run is dated Friday 8 October 2010 at 9:00am Pacific Time, stated in the article as 4:00pm GMT for UK and Europe, on Server 1. 9:00 PDT equals 16:00 UTC, so the GMT figure is consistent with the Pacific time. Article 1849's '16:00 European Time' wording is ambiguous and is not used as a UTC value.

Articles 1849 and 1850 are Spanish-language notices of the same two runs (Thu 7 Oct 2010 15:00 Pacific; Fri 8 Oct 2010 09:00 Pacific, Server 1). Their wording is forward-looking ('se llevara acabo', 'was to be held'), so they announce the schedule and do not confirm it ran.
The ghost pet for the party came from the Blackspore Pet Adoption Center.
The Blackspore Pet Adoption Center is run by Vusala and its pets are all ghosts. This is a general place article, not a party source.

The client names the event 'Ghostly Pet Party' (locale:14561) and its objective reads 'Bring your ghost pet and your favorite Halloween costume to this Blackspore bash!' (locale:14565, a quest_objective string).
The wiki Community Events page lists the Ghostly Pet Party as an event in Blackspore Swamp during Super Spooktacular, and says it is very similar to the Pet Party but themed around ghost pets.

Super Spooktacular is the parent Halloween holiday: 2009 (scheduled Oct 14 to Nov 11, 2009), 2010 (second year, October 2010 billed as Super Spooktacular month), 2013 (fourth annual, Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2013).

Article 1845 says October 2010 was Super Spooktacular month, with spooky community events planned every Thursday afternoon and Friday morning. This is month-level context only; it does not name the party as recurring.
The Super Spooktacular wiki category lists the parent holiday and its seasonal items. No item in that category is tied to the Ghostly Pet Party by any source, so items is empty.

This implies 2010 is the 2nd, 2011 the 3rd and 2012 the 4th, which conflicts with 2013 being the 4th. Unresolved; occurrences use the dated windows, not the numbers.
2012: no dated source. Wiki-only support (Candy Corn, Broomstick, Ghostly Raven). No occurrence added.
2010 exact event window is not stated; only 'October 2010' and the Oct 7-8 pet party are dated (article 1845).
Article 1861 is undated; its Pixiewood decoration and /scare facts are attributed to the event on the basis of the 'second year' wording, not a date.

Quests: no quest titles are confirmed by a source tied to the event. 'Spooktacular Balloons' (locale:91946) has an unconfirmed type and is only a reward name. Dance-off quest titles are wiki-only and excluded.
Bone Bog Cemetery / Blackspore battle instance and Pumpkin Prince battle come from the wiki only. The Bone Bog Cemetery Halloween Dance Party (article 484) is undated and not merged.
NPCs Lucinda, Ed Sullenfangs, Drake Sullenfangs and Jake Blackforest rest only on the pack's wiki summary; no source checked here. Excluded from npcs.
'Pumpkin King' (article 1862) and 'Prince Pumpkin' (article 1878) are probably Pumpkin Prince aliases. Madame/Madam Zelda spelling varies.
Parachute price 899 is from one unverified video frame; the wiki price field is blank. Price is null.
Items excluded for lack of event-specific dated source: Flaming Skull Wobblehead, Eyeball mount, Fog Machine.
Pack title 'Pixiewood decorations' is a location decoration fact merged into this event; key the pack to Super Spooktacular.
Live status 'yes' rests on dated official posts for 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2013 and locale:436400 ('Now Live!'). It means the event ran live historically, not that it is running now.

problems.issue: 2009 (First Annual Super Spooktacular) is left out as a 'planned window'. But article 476 (official, 'The Halloween event ran October 14 through November 11 and was free to all registered players') and the Ten Ton Hammer node 75739 ('Free Realms held its first Halloween-themed event, Super Spooktacular, which was scheduled to run from October 14 through November 11, 2009') both support a held 2009 run. The 2009 dates are the same as the planned window, and article 2949 itself calls 2013 the Fourth Annual, which makes 2009 the First Annual. Dropping 2009 leaves the 'annual' pattern resting on only two dated runs (2011, 2013).
problems.fix: Add occurrence 2009: October 14 to November 11, 2009 (First Annual), sources articleId=476 (ran/free to all registered players) and tentonhammer node/75739. Keep it apart from the 2009 'scheduled' wording, citing both.

problems.issue: The 'annual, October into November' rule is supported only by the wiki wording. The dated runs have different end dates (Nov 11, Nov 23, Nov 12) and the 2012 run is undated. The rule is a pattern, not a schedule, so it cannot be wired as a recurring rule without a per-year window.
problems.fix: Record the recurrence as the set of dated windows (2009: Oct 14-Nov 11; 2011: Oct 13-Nov 23; 2013: Oct 1-Nov 12), not as a fixed annual rule. Keep the wiki 'annual' wording marked as wiki-only.

problems.issue: Items with no year (Candy Corn, Broomstick, Ghostly Raven, Halloween Flooring, Halloween Wallpaper) are attached to the event without an occurrence. Their sources are wiki-only and say 2012 or are undated, so they cannot be tied to a 2011 or 2013 run in the calendar.
problems.fix: Mark these as undated, wiki-only event items and attach them to no occurrence until a dated source is found. The only item with a year is the Week #3 (10/15/13) marketplace group from the wiki, which sits in the 2013 run.

problems.issue: The 899 price rests on one unverified video frame (video:1TNyzyI62nc/00122.jpg). It should not be used as a scheduled price.

Article 1998 is in the index under its URL with &request_locale=en_US. The earlier critique that it was missing was wrong; the lookup returns its text. The four names are merged here because 1993 and 1998 give the same date, time and server for the UK and Europe session. That is a match on dates, times, server and camp name, not an explicit statement that they are one run.

Occurrences: one run, two sessions, both in January 2011. The 1993 article gives both (13 Jan 2011 Americas, 14 Jan 2011 UK and Europe). Article 2001 confirms the Americas session. The Europe session is confirmed by 1993 and 1998. Article 2000 is recorded as a Spanish announcement; its Europe time was not re-verified in this pass. No other month or year is found in the pack, so the event cannot be shown to recur.

Location conflict: articles 2000 and 2001 say north of the Villadelago teleport stone, article 1993 says north of the Lakeshore Warpstone, and article 1998 says north of the Lakeshore shores. The camp is named the same in all four. Zone recorded as Robgoblin Camp only; the exact spot is unresolved.
Recurrence not established. One run, two sessions, January 2011. The 1993 phrase 'our next community event' names other events, not a recurrence.
Live status: 'yes' rests on article 1993's past-tense 'was held' and article 2001's 'was held'. Those are announcements, and no post-event confirmation was found, so confidence stays moderate.

NPC: Palorroto (articles 2000 and 2001) is the mage trainer located at the Robgoblin Camp. The sources give his location, not a tie to the party, so he is left out of npcs. Glerga is not listed for the same reason.
Quests, items, rewards: none. No quest title or item is tied to this event by a source that names it, so those lists are empty.

Possible separate events not included: the birthday party (article 1293, locale:428066, Cakenstein's Last Stand) and the Kart Driver fireworks for a party at the Robgoblin Camp (locale:394604). Neither is tied to this event by a source that names it, so both are left out. Article 1293 needs checking to see whether it means this party or another.
The client strings (locale:31492, locale:9107) carry no date, so the match to the January 2011 run rests on the name alone.

open: Merging: the pack's single entry blends several years (2010 blog/dance, 2011 Gifting Basket, 2012 PS3 return, 2014 wiki). Occurrences are kept separate; items are not yet tagged by year, so do not treat the item list as one live set.
2011 is a single wiki mention (Cupid, Heart Critter); no article dates it. Weak lead only, not counted toward recurrence.
2012 date is inferred from article 2501's relative time ('6 months, 1 week ago' at the 2012-08-19 capture); it is approximate, not a stated date.
The 2010 blog date rests on the pack summary; full text of article 1003 was not checked. The dance is a community event (article 960; the pack's 957 citation is unverified).
2014 start date and Feb-Mar range are wiki-only.
Wiki Events page says a presents event was introduced in 2012, conflicting with the 2010/2011 mentions; unresolved.
Currency: station_cash labels come from wiki wording ('SC Marketplace'), not from stated prices. All prices are null; no price is in the pack.

Live: unsure. The rebuild's target year is not set. Not wireable as a yearly schedule until a second article-dated occurrence is found.

The event ran on Server 1 for the U.S./Latin America time slot (3pm Pacific) and the UK/Europe time slot.

During the Bristlewood Bash, Members got a teleport to the party from the Briarwood Party Planner, and anyone could reach it via the Game Guide calendar. Confirmed in the article 937 summary text ('Members get a teleport to the party from the Briarwood Party Planner, and anyone can reach it via the Game Guide calendar').
Mandy Vice, the Briarwood Party Planner, gives Members a teleport to the party and stands near the Briarwood warpstone.
The client holds the scheduled-event name 'Community Event: Bristlewood Bash'.
The Game Guide > Calendar route for community events is also described in articles 877, 1221, 1510 and 1888, which supports the mechanism generally.

evidence.claim: Job Sampling Week ran Nov 9-13, 2009, with one job trainer meeting per day: Mon Nov 9 Archer, Tue Nov 10 Wizard, Wed Nov 11 Medic, Thu Nov 12 Blacksmith, Fri Nov 13 Warrior. The dates come from article 580's summary in the pack, not a quote from the article, and the article date is null in the pack.
Job Sampling is a community event week in which SOE staff met players at job trainers on consecutive days to socialize, answer questions, trade equipment and duel.
Archer job sampling on Monday November 9th, meeting at Lugabow, the Archer trainer, near the Bandit Hideout.
Medic job sampling on Wednesday November 11th, meeting at Nurse Naia in Sanctuary, southeast of the great tree.
Blacksmith job sampling on Thursday November 12th, meeting at Smitty, the Blacksmith trainer, just outside the Singing Crystals Mine.
Warrior job sampling on Friday November 13th, meeting at Drill Sergeant Dewey, the Warrior trainer near the Snowhill Town Hall.
Wizard job sampling on Tuesday November 10th, meeting at Fizzlesticks, the Wizard trainer, near the Robgoblin Trove north of Lakeshore.
A different job was highlighted each day of the week, with a new article daily and players invited to the Job Sampling Community Events.
Past-tense confirmation that the event week ran: a different job was featured each day, and players were invited to join the Job Sampling Community Events.

evidence.claim: ConnecDING was announced by SOE as a social networking promotion: players who followed Free Realms on Twitter or Facebook could earn in-game prizes when SOE reached social networking goals. The article reports that SOE created Twitter and Facebook pages for Free Realms, EverQuest and EverQuest 2 as the vehicle for the promotion. The article is dated 2009-12-12; the pack gives no more precise date for page creation.
The article is a promotional news item and gives no quest, item, NPC or zone details for Free Realms, so no in-game content is tied to the promotion.

None names ConnecDING or a 2009-2010 promotion.

open: Merge risk: the 2013 '4th Birthday' post (articleId=2924) is treated as the same yearly program, but no source says so explicitly. The 2013 post gives no end date, schedule, or rewards.
Start dates for 2010, 2011 and 2012 are not stated; only end dates (May 10, May 18, May 24) are sourced. No fixed start rule can be wired yet.
The anniversary date is April 29 in 2010 (articleId=1267) and 2013 (articleId=2924) but April 28 in 2011 (articleId=2107). Use 'around April 28-29'.
May 18, 2011 end date comes from article summaries of 2099/2107; the full text was not re-read in this pass.

Summer Splash is a separate July 2009 Seaside event (articleId=137; locale:400812, 400900). locale:19968 ('Making this Birthday Bash a Summer Splash') links the two names and needs checking before any merge decision.
Birthday T-shirts (locale:5721, 5723) are in the client, but the wiki Category:Birthday Bash listing of six T-shirts by zone was not verified (the lookup query errored). Treat as unconfirmed.
Quest titles 'Birthday Bash!' (locale:29341) and 'Cakenstein Attacks!' (locale:4917) exist as text, but quest type is unconfirmed, so the quests list is empty.
Prices for Birthday Crates, balloon weapons and furniture other than the 1350 Station Cash bundle are unsourced and left null.
Glerga, Sal Monella, Bordon Cloo and Quills have bash-related dialog but no year; they are not placed in any occurrence.
The client zone list (locale 6707-6713) was not re-read; Snowhill rests on locale:6420 alone.
No 2014 or later occurrence is sourced. Live status 'yes' rests on dated posts for 2010-2013.

evidence.claim: 7-Eleven Day was a US promotion on July 11, 2013: guests visiting a participating 7-Eleven between 11AM and 7PM got a free small Slurpee.

Redeeming an SOE Game Card in store at a participating US 7-Eleven on 7-Eleven Day gave a bonus of 500 Station Cash (SC500). The bonus applied only to redemptions from 12:00AM to 11:59PM PDT on 7/11/13.
Game Cards could be bought at participating 7-Eleven stores until the offer ended at 11:59PM PDT on 7/11/13.
The article is a SOE news post. The pack's summary says it was posted about one week before a 2013-07-18 capture, so the 2013-07-04 date is inferred and not stated in the article.

Wiki promo image text names the event 7-Eleven Day, July 11th 2013, and says 'PLUS, FREE SLURPEE ON 7-11 DAY!', with 'DANCE PARTY' and 'KEEP DANCING ALL SUMMER LONG!' on the art. This ties the alias 7-11 Day to the event.

The client has no text naming 7-Eleven Day. The only client hit for 7-Eleven or Slurpee is locale:4889 ('Cruise around Free Realms on this exclusive T-Rex Ride from 7-Eleven.'). It names the retailer, not this event, so it is not tied to the event.
A separate 7-Eleven double Station Cash promotion (article 2806) and a July 4, 2013 SC1000 promotion (article 2943) are different offers, and the pack should not merge them into this event.
